cognate: *deh3- + *dʰugh2tḗr- (acc.) + dative of the groom, often with reflexive possessive *swo-/*swe- and a predicate 'as wife' (*gʷen-): Gk δίδωμι θυγατέρα ἥν / Skt dā svāṃ duhitaram / Arm tam zdowstr iwr (i) knowtʻiwn|kin
drift_or_renewal: ON renews the verb with gipta (from gefa, *gʰebʰ-) but keeps dóttir + reflexive sinn + dative of the husband (gipti døtr sinar jorlom sínom)
shared_syntax: father (subject) gives his own daughter (acc.) to a man (dat.), Armenian and Sanskrit adding the role noun 'wife' (kin/knowtʻiwn; patnī), Greek prose γυναῖκα
context: dynastic marriage alliances in historiography/epic: Armenian kings and nobles (Faustos, Movses), Greek tyrants (Thucydides) and Homer's Lycian king giving his daughter to Bellerophon, Indic epic kings giving daughters, Norse kings giving daughters to earls
phrase: 'X gave his own daughter to Y (as wife)'
note: Exact verb+object+possessive cognate set in Greek, Sanskrit and Armenian in the same legal-dynastic frame (marriage by the father's gift, cf. Benveniste on IE marriage terms: the woman is 'given', the man 'leads'). Low because 'give one's daughter in marriage' is typologically universal (also Semitic, and Classical Armenian historiography is Bible-influenced), so the match shows inherited legal wording only weakly; the Homeric formula δίδου δ' ὅ γε θυγατέρα ἥν is the strongest early witness.

search_lead.cognate: *ḱlew- 'hear / be heard' + *h1nómn̥ 'name': MIr docluinfidear (fut. pass. 3sg of (ro)cluinethar, 'will be heard') ... ainm; Ved. śrávas-/śruta- + nā́man; Gk κλυτός + ὄνομα
search_lead.argument: The druid's birth prophecy 'the name of the son born tonight will be heard throughout Ireland' joins the reflex of *ḱlew- with *h1nómn̥ in the theme of a newborn's future fame; Vedic has 'the son set a name for fame' (sūnúḥ śrávase nā́ma dadhé) and Homer the formula ὄνομα κλυτόν. The Irish is Middle Irish prose and the phrasing is a natural one, so this is a lead, not a claim; the slab's Norse partner (Laxdæla heyra ... í nótt borinn) has the same scene (child born tonight, report heard) but non-cognate heyra.

near_miss.lead: kin-pair chain as 'nobody at all': ORV брат брату ... ни отьць сынови ни мати дъчери; Arm ոչ ... որդի հաւր, ոչ քոյր ... եղբաւր; OIr do-ceiled athair ar a mac ⁊ máthair ar ingin (cf. Hes. Op. 182ff, Vsp. 45)
near_miss.why_not: Same pairs (father/son, mother/daughter) but contexts differ (famine, massacre, secrecy) and the chain is identical to Luke 12:53 / Micah 7:6, which plausibly shaped the Christian ORV and Armenian texts; universal polar merism.
